newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Rival workers fight, keep Chittagong port shut.
newsitem.headline: Rival workers fight, keep Chittagong port shut.

text.p: Ten people were injured on Saturday as rival workers at Bangladesh's main Chittagong port clashed during a labour stoppage that suspended cargo handling for a third day, port officials said.
The officials described the situation as tense as the rival workers were fighting outside the port. "We can hear explosions of home-made bombs," said one official at the port.
Nearly 8,000 dock workers walked off their jobs on Thursday following a labour dispute over an attempt to allow coaster hatch workers to work on the jetties by the port authorities.
"At least 10 workers on both sides have been injured and two of them admitted to a clinic," said a dock labour leader.
Coaster hatch workers, who are not listed as port workers, normally handle only cargo for small local ships outside the port. These workers are now seeking jobs in the port, the officials said.
The Chittagong Port Authority was holding meeting with unions of dock workers and coaster hatch workers to solve the dispute, the officials added.
"We will not resume work unless the move to allow the coaster hatch workers to work on the jetties stop," a leader of Dock Workers Union said.
The officials said the registered dock workers feared losing jobs if the coaster hatch workers were allowed to work on the jetties.
There are about 30 ships at the port jetties and at the outer anchorage awaiting unloading of high speed diesel, crude oil, cement, soyabean oil and general cargo, the port officials said.
